transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been really struggling with my eating habits lately. I keep having these episodes where I completely lose control and eat an unusually large amount of food in one sitting. It's really hard to talk about, but I just don't know how to stop it.
After these episodes of overeating, do you engage in any specific behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, misusing laxatives, or excessive exercising?

It's really hard to admit, but yes, I do. Out of panic, I will force myself to throw up, take laxatives, or fast and exercise for hours to try to undo the eating. I just feel so desperate to prevent any weight gain after it happens.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Bulimia Nervosa]. The patient confirmed engaging in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise to prevent weight gain following binge episodes. These compensatory behaviors are the distinguishing feature of Bulimia Nervosa, effectively ruling out Binge-Eating Disorder.
